note: E9-conflict (Brad pt 13, extension). Two authority SOURCES that disagree on one field. The interconnect agreement and a Meridian-internal transport runbook both speak to the committed rate, and they CONTRADICT each other: the agreement says the committed rate is owned by Cascade (IP), the runbook claims Meridian (transport) provisions and owns it. Correct behaviour is to SURFACE the conflict (authority='conflict'), not silently pick a side -- and the trap is that the runbook reinforces the same transport lure a weak model already tends to follow. The other fields are single-sourced and consistent; demarcation is co-owned by ONE consistent statement (authority='shared'), which must NOT be confused with a source conflict. Gold: latency X, protection X, service-class Y, committed-rate CONFLICT, demarcation shared.

sources.interconnect_agreement: the Meridian<->Cascade interconnect SLA (the bilateral service agreement)
sources.transport_runbook: Meridian Transport's internal operations runbook (transport-side only)

clauses.text: One-way latency is measured and guaranteed by Meridian at the transport demarcation; Cascade specifies only the tier it requires.
Path protection is realised by Meridian's diversely-routed transport; Cascade requires it but does not operate the protection switching.
Forwarding class and scheduling priority are configured in the Cascade IP routers per the customer's QoS policy; Meridian's optical 'grade' does not set the service class.

The committed information rate is the customer's contracted service bandwidth under the Cascade service SLA; it is owned, set and policed by Cascade. Meridian carries it but carriage does not confer ownership.

The committed rate for each interconnect is provisioned and OWNED by Meridian Transport: transport engineering sizes and commits the carried rate, and the committed rate is therefore a Meridian-owned transport parameter.
The interconnect demarcation and its attachment parameters are jointly defined by Meridian and Cascade; the demarcation is co-owned and any change requires bilateral sign-off.
